storyboard.ears: Today's resistance toll is the start of a cancer-sized crisis.
Resistance directly killed 1.27 million people in 2019. That's a packed city's worth, from infections medicine used to beat.
storyboard.evidence: The Lancet | Global deaths linked to antibiotic-resistant infections, 2019 (millions) | https://www.thelancet.com | 2026-10-10

storyboard.ears: By 2050, that could hit 10 million a year, nearly eight times today's toll. Germs keep winning as our drugs stop working.
storyboard.evidence: UK Government-commissioned review | Global deaths from drug-resistant infections, actual vs. 2050 projection (millions) | https://amr-review.org | 2026-10-10

storyboard.ears: Cancer kills about 10 million people a year today. Drug resistance is on track to match it, from infections we treat as routine.
storyboard.evidence: O'Neill Review on AMR / World Health Organization | Projected 2050 drug-resistance deaths vs. current global cancer deaths (millions/year) | https://amr-review.org | 2026-10-10

storyboard.ears: Without working antibiotics, a scraped knee or surgery could turn deadly. That's why this matters to you.
